title: Stock-Split Watch: Is Caterpillar Next?
author: Scott Levine
description: Caterpillar stock has surged 76% over the past year, touching an all-time high of $1,064 in late June, but is now trading around $820 after a 23% pullback from its peak. While the company has a history of stock splits (five times since 1976), analysts believe a near-term split is unlikely given current share prices. Strong financial performance, including record 2025 revenue of $67.6 billion and Q2 2026 revenue growth of 24%, supports the company's position as a leading industrial stock.

insights.sentiment_reasoning: Strong year-over-year financial performance with record revenue ($67.6B in 2025, 24% growth in Q2 2026), record backlog ($72B), and exceptional free cash flow growth (118% YoY). Stock outperformed S&P 500 significantly over the past year despite recent 23% pullback from all-time highs. Company is positioned well for future growth.

title: Caterpillar Inc. (CAT) Is a Trending Stock: Facts to Know Before Betting on It
author: Zacks.Com
description: Caterpillar has been trending on Zacks.com's most searched stocks list. The construction equipment company shows strong earnings growth expectations with consensus estimates indicating +43.6% year-over-year growth for the current fiscal year and +20.5% for the next year. Revenue is also projected to grow +17.4% and +10.9% respectively. The company has consistently beaten earnings and revenue estimates over the trailing four quarters. However, Caterpillar is trading at a premium valuation relative to peers, receiving an F grade on the Zacks Value Style Score. Despite the valuation concerns, the stock holds a Zacks Rank #1 (Strong Buy) rating, suggesting potential near-term outperformance.

insights.sentiment_reasoning: Strong earnings growth expectations (+43.6% current year, +20.5% next year), consistent beat history on both earnings and revenue estimates over four quarters, and Zacks Rank #1 (Strong Buy) rating support positive sentiment. However, this is tempered by premium valuation (F grade on Value Style Score), indicating the stock may be overpriced relative to peers.

title: Looking for Industrial Products Stocks? The Zacks Rank Can Help You Find Winners
author: Zacks.Com
description: The article explains how the Zacks Rank stock-rating system helps investors identify winning stocks by analyzing earnings estimate revisions. It highlights Caterpillar (CAT) as a newly added Zacks Rank #1 (Strong Buy) stock, noting that 13 analysts raised earnings estimates in the last 60 days, with expected earnings growth of 43.6% for fiscal 2026. The Zacks Rank has historically beaten the market with an average annual return of +23.8% over the past 32 years.

The company shows strong fundamentals with expected earnings growth of 43.6% and revenue growth of 17.4% for fiscal 2026, plus an average earnings surprise of 18.1% and positive price momentum of +2.8% over four weeks.

title: Is Caterpillar the Best Industrials Stock to Buy Right Now?
author: Catie Hogan
description: Caterpillar delivered one of its strongest quarters, with Q2 2026 revenue up 24% to $20.5 billion and a record $72 billion backlog driven by AI infrastructure demand. The company's EPS reached $7.77, and analysts project significant upside with an average price target of $975 versus the current $803 price. However, the trailing P/E ratio above 35 reflects elevated valuation, though justified by multiyear demand visibility and reduced cyclicality.

insights.sentiment_reasoning: Strong quarterly performance with 24% revenue growth, record $72 billion backlog, robust EPS of $7.77, and significant AI-driven demand providing multiyear revenue visibility. Analysts project substantial upside potential with average price target of $975 versus current $803 price, indicating confidence in future growth trajectory.

title: Market Indexes Fall Again as the 30-Year Yield Hits a 2004 High
author: Anders Bylund
description: U.S. stock markets declined for a second consecutive day as Treasury yields reached multidecade highs and geopolitical tensions drove oil prices up. The Nasdaq fell 0.8%, the Dow 0.6%, and the S&P 500 0.5%. Oracle's data center project faced delays due to power supply issues, while Meta gained on AI optimism. The U.S. and China extended their trade truce by only two months instead of the three years China sought.
